brief: BofA's monthly CTA Design Impact Monitor attributes trend-following performance dispersion to four backtested design levers, ranked universe selection and trend speed first, risk budget next, volatility reactivity last. The chain runs from dispersion to design: cross-model dispersion sets how much construction matters, so when dispersion compresses manager outcomes converge. Dispersion eased from its first-half 2026 highs into August but stayed above its long-run median and below the 2018 and 2020 extremes, so design still separates managers. In August the wide July slow-versus-fast divide narrowed. Fast trend kept lagging the baseline, slow trend performed broadly in line with it, and universe selection became the largest relative effect with small universes the biggest detractor, equity and fixed income overweights modest detractors. Over the quarter the divide holds. Fast trend has detracted in four consecutive periods since 4Q25 and sits 4.6% below baseline quarter to date, slow trend is ahead, and small universe and equity overweight reversed strong 2Q26 gains into quarter-to-date losses of 2.9% and 2.1%. On 12-month rolling data slow sits above its long-run median and fast materially below. All model results are backtested.
